summary: This article explains how skin protects the body, keeps it at the right temperature, senses touch, and heals itself after a small cut.
introduce: Write “Problem” and “Solution” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to think of a problem people face in daily life and one way to fix it. Explain that as they read “Skin: Your Body's Shield”, they will look for the main problem and how it is solved.

keyTerms.def: a tiny part in the skin that picks up feelings like pressure or heat
having enough water inside to work properly
to change from a liquid into a gas and disappear into the air

challengeTerms.def: the thin outer layer of the skin
the thicker layer of skin beneath the epidermis, where nerves and sweat glands are found
to grow back or form again after being damaged

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that skin does more jobs for the body than most people realize? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how skin helps regulate body temperature when a person is too hot and when a person is too cold.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review receptor, hydrated, and evaporate, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use epidermis, dermis, and regenerate in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
